patterns.what_worked: Reading the engine before writing the class side: practice.lua's contract block and practice_ui.lua's scenario_context/drill_list_press showed the real ctx shape (resources + stripped cooldown names, last_action nil on a drill press), which forced the drills to be moment judges and the class to gather its own state. Mutation proofs on /tmp/opencode copies caught the two dead helpers (the wiring check counts a qualified call inside the owning module) and proved every band is pinned.
patterns.what_was_hard: The audit's drill bands were written for a press-the-player-action model, but the engine's drill press carries no action, so the bands had to be re-mapped to moment judgements (documented in bench/druid_drills_2026-10-19.md section 3). The Omen-ICD probe has no client-side source and rests on an UNCONFIRMED assumption (the ICD and the proc buff share one window).
patterns.skill_gap: Reconciling an audit spec written against a hypothetical harness with the harness that actually exists: the ctx contract should have been read from practice.lua/practice_ui.lua first, before designing the drills.
